idiom_name: Enumerable#flat_map / each_slice / slice_before over a lazy enumerator
implementation_notes: Ruby's Enumerable is the splitter: flat_map maps a composite to its parts (returning [] to emit nothing), each_slice(n) chunks it, and slice_before/slice_when split on a delimiter or a predicate boundary, while .lazy keeps the pipeline streaming so a huge composite is never materialised. There is no role structure to write - the Enumerable methods are the pattern - and the send loop publishes the parts with correlation and sequence keys merged into each part's hash, because no framework adds them. A hand-written Splitter class earns its place only when several payload formats must be registered and chosen at runtime.
pitfalls: each_slice yields Arrays (batches) while flat_map yields single elements - swapping them publishes batches where single-item messages are expected.
Lazy enumerators are single-use and re-entrancy is not safe: a stored Enumerator that was consumed yields nothing on the second pass.
Ruby has no default parallel fan-out; threads or Ractors must be added deliberately, and a part hash shared between threads must not be mutated.
